Both defects are in the generator, and every agent file ethos emits carries them.

DEFECT 1 — the reporting line is emitted twice, in two different vocabularies.

  internal/hook/generate_agents.go:445
    return fmt.Sprintf(\"You report to %s.\", joinWithOxford(names))
    -> IDENTITY form  ('Claude Agento (claude)')

  internal/hook/generate_agents.go:727
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, \"You report to %s. These are not yours:\\n\\n\", joinWithOxford(targets))
    -> ROLE-SLUG form ('coo', 'vision-keeper')

Both fire for the same agent, land ~50 lines apart in the output, and neither knows about the other. A reader sees two different principals named for one relationship. Observed in all five of xboing's agent files:

  latex-tech-architect.md  :24 claude / :73 coo
  jck.md                   :24 claude / :138 coo
  jdc.md                   :23 jck    / :96 vision-keeper
  gjm.md                   :23 jck    / :106 vision-keeper
  sjl.md                   :23 jck    / :97 vision-keeper

ROOT CAUSE: no single helper owns how a reporting relationship is written. There is a THIRD renderer of the same sentence at internal/hook/subagent_start.go:864 —
  fmt.Sprintf(\"You report to %s (%s).\", parentIdentity.Name, parentIdentity.Handle)
so the fact is spelled three times across two files. Fixing only the two in generate_agents.go leaves the drift vector in place.

DEFECT 2 — comma-spliced identity sentence.

  internal/hook/generate_agents.go:670
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, \"\\nYou are %s (%s), %s.\\n\", id.Name, id.Handle, firstLine)
  internal/hook/persona.go:42
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, \"You are %s (%s), %s.\", id.Name, id.Handle, first)

Both interpolate a description authored as a standalone capitalized sentence into a ', %s.' template, yielding:

  You are LaTeX Technical Architect (latex-tech-architect), Produces technical
  documentation in LaTeX — architecture docs, design reviews, ...

  You are Glenford J. Myers (gjm), Software testing pioneer. Wrote *The Art of
  Software Testing* in 1979 — ...

Fix needs a connective ('who produces') or a period and a new sentence, applied at both call sites — same duplication problem as defect 1.

TESTS THAT PIN THE CURRENT STRINGS and will need updating:
  internal/hook/subagent_start_test.go:117   asserts 'You report to Claude Agento (claude).'
  internal/hook/subagent_start_test.go:1133  asserts NotContains 'You report to'
  internal/hook/subprocess_test.go:617       asserts NotContains 'You report to'

NOT A DEFECT: 'Claude Agento' is a real identity name (confirmed via 'ethos whoami'), not a typo. Copilot guessed otherwise; do not 'correct' it or the identity-to-handle mapping breaks.

WHY THIS COULD NOT BE FIXED DOWNSTREAM: these files regenerate from team data at SessionStart, so a hand-edit to any artifact is reverted next session, and editing one of five would leave the set inconsistent." --acceptance="Regenerated .claude/agents/*.md files state the reporting relationship once, in one vocabulary, and open with a grammatical identity sentence. ---
name: file-tool-beads-in-the-tool-project
description: Never file a bead about ethos/bd/quarry/lux in xboing — use `bd -C <tool-repo> create` so it lands in that tool's project
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A bead about a *tool's* defect goes in that tool's beads project, never in
xboing. Use the `-C` flag — it works like `git -C`:

```bash
bd -C ~/Coding/punt-labs/ethos create --title=... --type=bug
```

IDs then come out correctly prefixed (`ethos-i3a2`, not `xboing-...`).

**Why:** the user maintains many repos and only wants xboing's tracker to hold
xboing's work. Commit e2ae878 (#221), "split the ethos backlog upstream, keep
what is actually xboing's", exists purely to undo a previous round of this.
The convention is also recorded inside existing beads — `xboing-c-xzt` notes
"MOVED UPSTREAM as ethos-bfml". Filing tool bugs locally forces the user to
re-sort the backlog by hand.

**How to apply:** before `bd create`, ask whose code the defect is in. If it
isn't `xboing`'s own source, config, or docs, add `-C <that repo>`. If the
right home is unclear, don't file — mention it instead. See
[[verify-a-defect-reproduces-before-filing]].

---
name: verify-a-defect-reproduces-before-filing
description: Before calling something a tool bug, check it reproduces outside this repo — usually it's local config or data, not the tool
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Before filing a defect against a shared tool, **prove it reproduces outside
xboing**. The tool ships test fixtures and other repos use it; check those
first.

**Why:** the user pushed back with "I have no other agent/project that is
having so many issues with ethos, so I am not convinced you are even finding
bugs vs. just using it wrong." That was correct. Two findings I had escalated
from a Copilot review both evaporated on one grep of ethos's own fixtures:

- The "comma-spliced identity sentence" — ethos's fixtures author descriptions
  as *clauses* (`"a Go specialist on the Punt Labs engineering team"`) that
  slot into `"You are %s (%s), %s."` correctly. Xboing wrote its descriptions
  as standalone capitalized sentences. Bad input, correct template.
- The "duplicated You report to line" — all 18 ethos fixture agents have
  exactly one. Xboing has two because a block guarded by `len(antiResps) > 0`
  fires only when the report target's role defines responsibilities. Xboing's
  team does; the fixtures don't. Intended behavior on a path xboing exercises.

A reviewer flagging something in one artifact is a *hypothesis*, not a
confirmed defect — over-generalizing from a single file is what produced both
errors.

**How to apply:** grep the tool's `tests/`, `fixtures/`, or a sibling repo for
the same pattern. Same result elsewhere → tool bug. Only here → our config or
data, so fix it here or just say so. When it's our own content, prefer telling
the user over filing anything. See
[[file-tool-beads-in-the-tool-project]] and [[report-data-not-rendering]].
